title: Car seat & stroller safety picks
summary: Ranked by independent crash testing, recall records and safety features. No U.S. government crash rating exists for car seats: NHTSA's stars rate ease of use, not safety. Every seat sold legally passes the federal crash test; the rankings below separate good from better, not safe from unsafe.
caveats: When Consumer Reports and BabyGearLab disagree, both are shown: treat both seats as safe and decide on fit, installation, rear-facing limits, load leg and recalls.
"No recall found" was checked against NHTSA and CPSC recall data on 2026-10-03; still check your exact model number and manufacture date at NHTSA.gov/recalls.
Current NHTSA Ease-of-Use stars could not be retrieved for 2026 models; Consumer Reports crash grades are paywalled.

dates.label: Target car seat trade-in ends (20% Target Circle bonus)
Seats made on or after this date must meet the FMVSS 213a side-impact and 213b frontal rules

picks.name: Nuna PIPA rx
picks.why: Lowest crash forces BabyGearLab has recorded (crash 9.0). Load leg + rebound panel, rigid LATCH, baseless belt install, FAA label. Fits the most compact strollers (TRVL natively; Minu V3, YOYO, Butterfly via adapter).

picks.name: Chicco KeyFit Max (replaces KeyFit 35)
picks.why: Consumer Reports gave the KeyFit 35 5/5 for ease of use and 5/5 for belt fit; Wirecutter's runner-up is the KeyFit Max, which replaced it. Chicco states the Max meets FMVSS 213a + 213b and carries the FAA label.
flags: No confirmed adapter for most premium compact strollers

picks.name: Britax Willow S
picks.why: BabyGearLab Best Budget, crash 7.8, anti-rebound bar. Not part of Britax's 2026 B-Safe handle recall (26C-006).

picks.name: Clek Liing
picks.why: Wirecutter's rigid-LATCH pick; load leg; BabyGearLab crash 7.5 vs a 7.2 group average.
flags: Recalls cover seats made before Sep 2020 / Feb 2021: check your date label

picks.name: Graco SnugRide SnugFit 35 DLX
picks.why: Wirecutter's longtime top pick; anti-rebound bar; 30 lb limit (per Wirecutter). Graco says no other SnugRide is affected by the Turn & Slide recall.

picks.name: Graco Extend2Fit / Extend2Fit 3-in-1
picks.why: Most agreement across sources: Wirecutter top pick, Consumer Reports crash "Best" (3-in-1), BabyGearLab crash 8.5. Rear-faces to 50 lb, as the AAP advises.
flags: 16C-002 only covers seats made Nov 27 2015–Jan 20 2016 (misplaced recline label)

picks.name: Graco 4Ever DLX
picks.why: Tied for BabyGearLab's top convertible crash score (8.7, with Turn2Me and UPPAbaby Rove); Best for Most Families. Only pick with verified NHTSA stars (2021: RF 4, FF 5, booster 4).
flags: BabyGearLab convertible page last updated Sep 2025

picks.name: Britax Poplar / Poplar S
picks.why: Consumer Reports 2026 Value Pick, "excellent crash protection"; under 17 in wide (3-across); rear-faces to 50 lb; 10-year life.
flags: Rear-facing recline may be too upright for newborns

picks.name: Chicco Fit360 or Graco Turn2Me (rotating)
picks.why: Fit360: Consumer Reports 2026 Top Pick with its highest crash rating, "one of the easiest" installs in BabyGearLab testing. Turn2Me: BabyGearLab crash 8.7 with among the lowest head-injury readings.
flags: Conflict: BabyGearLab rated Fit360 crash 7.1 (below average)

picks.name: Nuna RAVA Next
picks.why: BabyGearLab overall 80, crash 8.4; rear-faces to 50 lb. Recall 24C-002 covers only original RAVAs made before Oct 26, 2023.

picks.name: UPPAbaby Minu V3
picks.why: BabyGearLab Best Overall travel stroller (81); recommended by Consumer Reports. ~17 lb. Adapters for Mesa, Nuna PIPA, Maxi-Cosi, Clek.

picks.name: Nuna TRVL lx
picks.why: Consumer Reports recommended, 14.6 lb; the original TRVL scored 9.0 for maneuverability at BabyGearLab, among the best. Nuna PIPA clicks in with no adapter.
flags: Fold exceeds cabin guidelines: plan to gate-check

picks.name: gb Pockit+ All-City
picks.why: Smallest fold BabyGearLab measured (score 73, Most Compact), 13.1 lb; includes Cybex car seat adapters.

picks.name: Stokke YOYO³ / Bugaboo Butterfly 2
picks.why: Cabin-size folds. BabyGearLab now scores the YOYO 3 just 56 overall (14.5 lb, $500); takes Nuna PIPA, Cybex, Maxi-Cosi and Clek seats via adapters.
flags: YOYO³ parking-brake recall Nov 2024: check serial

picks.name: Chicco Bravo Trio (newborn travel system)
picks.why: Consumer Reports' top-rated travel system for newborns; KeyFit 30 clicks in natively.

picks.name: Nuna MIXX next + PIPA rx (or SWIV + PIPA aire rx)
picks.why: Pairs the best-crash-testing infant seat (BabyGearLab 9.0) with a full-size stroller; adapter in the box. Consumer Reports' 2026 Top Pick travel system is the SWIV + PIPA aire rx.

picks.name: Britax Willow Brook S+
picks.why: Willow S seat is BabyGearLab's Best Budget infant seat (crash 7.8, anti-rebound bar); clicks in natively. Not part of Britax's B-Safe handle recall.

picks.name: Chicco Bravo Trio / Corso with KeyFit
picks.why: Native click-in, no adapter; Consumer Reports rates KeyFit installation 5/5. LE/Primo versions include the KeyFit Max (maker-stated 213a + 213b).
flags: Conflict: middling BabyGearLab crash scores for KeyFit

picks.name: Evenflo Shyft DualRide (car seat that becomes a stroller)
picks.why: Best integrated option: BabyGearLab 71 overall, crash 6.8 ("slightly above average… better than" the Doona), Top Pick for urban families who walk. Wheel frame stays in the car.
flags: Frame works only with this seat
Weight: 20.1 lb measured vs 29 lb listed

picks.name: Graco Modes 3 Lite DLX + SnugRide 35 Lite LX (budget)
picks.why: Cheapest well-evidenced option: BabyGearLab "Best Crash Test on the Tightest Budget" (seat crash 7.4); native click-in.
flags: Avoid the Modes Nest with Turn & Slide (recall 26C-003)

avoid.name: Evenflo REO by Revolve360
avoid.detail: NHTSA 26C-004 (Jul 2026): headrest shifted in NHTSA's own crash test; 59,661 seats; no fix yet.

avoid.name: Doona (2020–2024 seats)
avoid.detail: Open NHTSA investigation PE26005 (Jul 2026) into carry handles coming off; no recall yet. Pages claiming a Doona "CPSC recall 25-784" are false.

avoid.name: Graco SnugRide Turn & Slide (incl. Modes Nest travel system 7DP08NRI)
avoid.detail: NHTSA 26C-003 (Apr 2026): carrier may detach from base in a crash; free replacement.

avoid.name: Evenflo Revolve180 LiteMax NXT
avoid.detail: NHTSA 26C-005 (Aug 2026): recline indicator leaves baby too upright; ~23,000–35,951 seats (sources differ); repair kit expected Nov 2026.

avoid.name: Britax B-Safe Gen2 / 35 / Ultra, Endeavours
avoid.detail: NHTSA 26C-006 (Aug 2026): carry handle can partially detach; 114,660 seats made 2020–21; remedy still being developed, owner letters by Oct 19.

avoid.name: Joolz Aer2 car seat adapters
avoid.detail: CPSC (Jun 2026): adapters can fail to properly attach and the car seat can fall; refund.

avoid.name: UPPAbaby Mesa V3 and Doona
avoid.detail: Lowest crash results in BabyGearLab's 2026 infant seat tests. Doona also has an open NHTSA investigation (PE26005) into carry handles detaching.

avoid.name: Maxi-Cosi Emme 360
avoid.detail: Consumer Reports crash rating "Basic"; shell didn't stay well attached to the base forward-facing.

avoid.name: Unbranded or marketplace car seats
avoid.detail: Counterfeit seats sold on Temu and Amazon weren't certified for U.S. use. Buy from authorized retailers and check the FMVSS 213 label.

verified: Every cited page was opened and checked against each claim on 2026-10-03; recalls were checked in NHTSA's recall data and CPSC's recall API. Corrections from that check are applied below.

trust.name: Consumer Reports
trust.detail: Nonprofit, no ads, buys seats at retail. Crash-tests at 35 mph with a simulated front seatback (federal test: 30 mph, none); ~130 infant-seat tests; protocol reviewed by an outside biomechanics expert. Limits: single runs, crash grades paywalled, withdrew a faulty side-impact report in Jan 2007.

trust.name: BabyGearLab
trust.detail: Review site founded by a pediatrician, part of the GearLab group, paid through affiliate links; says it buys every product. Pays MGA Research (an NHTSA contract lab) for a 32 mph sled test, apparently one run per seat; full protocol unpublished; no peer review. Treat big gaps (e.g. 9.0 vs 4.6) as meaningful, small ones as noise.

trust.name: Wirecutter (NYT)
trust.detail: Part of The New York Times. Stopped its own crash tests after 2018 on expert advice that they can't separate well-engineered seats; relies on installs and certified car seat technicians.

trust.name: NHTSA
trust.weight: Authoritative for recalls and legal minimums
trust.detail: Recalls and investigations are the most reliable red flags. Ease-of-Use stars measure "ease of use, not safety"; NHTSA dropped crash-based seat ratings in 2005. Every seat must pass FMVSS 213 (pass/fail).

trust.name: Peer-reviewed research
trust.detail: CHOP sled studies support load legs (lower head-injury measures). Rear-facing longer is still advised, but the best-known field study was retracted in 2017; support now comes from lab and non-U.S. data. No study shows CR or BabyGearLab ratings predict real-world injuries.
